title: OTel GenAI semantic conventions
summary: The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions define shared span names, attributes and metrics for model calls, agents, tools, workflows and MCP, so any instrumented app can feed any compatible backend. All of it has status Development.
useIf: You instrument LLM or agent code and want dashboards, alerts and backends that survive a change of framework or vendor.
avoidIf: You treat attribute and metric names as frozen: they are still changing and moved repositories on 2026-05-05.

explain.md: The conventions cover client inference spans and metrics, model spans, agent and framework spans, events, exceptions, token metrics and MCP. Every part carries the status **Development** (checked 2026-10-13). The docs moved from `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions` to `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` (PR 3696, merged 2026-05-05). Release v1.41.1 (2026-05-11) of the old repository still holds the full text, v1.42.0 (2026-06-12) holds only a Moved stub, and opentelemetry.io shows Moved. The new repository has no tags or releases, so pin by commit [[r1]].

explain.md: Required on inference spans are `gen_ai.operation.name` and `gen_ai.provider.name`. Metric names have churned: the v1.41 text defined a `gen_ai.client.token.usage` histogram that no longer appears in the new repository, which defines token **counters** (`gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*`) instead, while Agent Framework's docs still list `gen_ai.client.token.usage` [[r5]] [[r10]]. Check what your build and backend emit before you build dashboards.

explain.title: Development status, checked 2026-10-13
explain.md: Older v1.41.1 text said instrumentations that emitted v1.36.0 or earlier must not change their defaults and should offer `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`. The new docs do not repeat this, so whether instrumentations still honor it is UNVERIFIED.

pitfalls.symptom: A token panel built on `gen_ai.client.token.usage` goes blank after an upgrade
pitfalls.cause: Metric names changed: newer conventions use `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*` counters
pitfalls.fix: Inspect the names your build emits, pin versions and keep dashboard queries in one mapping layer [[r5]]

pitfalls.symptom: Documentation links lead to a Moved page
pitfalls.cause: The conventions moved repositories on 2026-05-05 and some docs still link the old URL
pitfalls.fix: Cite and pin the semantic-conventions-genai repository by commit [[r1]]

pitfalls.symptom: Traces show up in a backend but cost and agent views stay empty
pitfalls.cause: The backend expects attribute names your instrumentation does not set, such as `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`
pitfalls.fix: Verify with a query on a few spans, then add the missing attributes or map them in a collector [[r14]]

scenarios.title: Six teams, two backends, one telemetry standard
scenarios.situation: Six teams build agents on different frameworks. Two backends are in use. A platform team wants shared dashboards and alerts.
unknowns: Which frameworks already emit GenAI spans?
Which backends map OTel attributes natively?
scenarios.question: What standard do you set?

options.name: Adopt the OTel GenAI names, pin a version and wrap custom spans in one internal helper
options.why: Shared names make dashboards portable and the helper absorbs renames.
options.tradeoff: You must track the repository and test upgrades.

options.name: Let each team choose its own attribute names
options.why: No shared dashboard or alert can work across teams.

options.name: Adopt one vendor SDK's attributes for everyone
options.why: Fast to roll out with one backend's features.
options.tradeoff: Lock-in and poor fit for the second backend.

flips.then: Snapshot the convention version and run a collector transform to a stable internal schema.

flips.if: Only one team and one backend exist

scenarios.takeaway: Standardize on shared names and isolate change in one place.

scenarios.title: A dashboard goes blank after a framework upgrade
scenarios.situation: A token usage dashboard stopped showing data the day a framework was upgraded. Traces still arrive.
unknowns: Which metric names does the new build emit?
Do other panels use the same names?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: List the emitted metric names, update the queries and keep names in one mapping layer
options.why: It fixes the cause and prevents repeats when names change again.
options.tradeoff: A small amount of indirection to maintain.

options.name: Roll back the framework
options.tradeoff: Delays the upgrade and the next one breaks it again.

options.name: Assume the metrics are lost and rebuild the dashboard from traces
options.why: Traces are sampled, so totals will be wrong.
options.tradeoff: Traces help explain a spike but are not a source for totals.

flips.if: The new names are documented and stable
Both old and new builds run together
flips.then: Query both names during the migration.

scenarios.takeaway: Verify what is emitted before trusting a dashboard.

quiz.q: What is the status of the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions as of 2026-10-13?
quiz.explain: All GenAI conventions carry the status Development. They moved to the semantic-conventions-genai repository on 2026-05-05 and have no tagged release yet, so names can change.

quiz.q: Match each attribute to the question it helps answer.

pairs.r: Is this a chat, tool or agent step?
How much input hit the cache?
Which session did this run belong to?

quiz.explain: Operation name classifies the work, finish reasons reveal truncation, cache-read tokens measure caching and the conversation id groups runs.

quiz.q: After an upgrade, a panel based on `gen_ai.client.token.usage` is empty although traces arrive. What is the most likely cause?
options: The backend dropped traces older than a day
The build emits different metric names, such as token counters under `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*`
quiz.explain: Metric names differ between convention versions and builds. Metrics are not sampled, retention does not explain a blank live panel and content capture does not affect metric names.
